_why: An inert fix is one that EXISTS and is NOT IN EFFECT. It passes every
review, every test, every 'did you do it' question -- and changes nothing,
because the copy carrying it is not the copy being loaded, or the process
that would read it started before it was written.
Two instances found on 2026-08-18, hours apart, neither caught by any
1. The whose-window field for the hook-timing log lived in two of eight
loadable copies of _lib.sh. Every window on one side of the house
loaded a copy without it, so the log stayed unable to name its writer.
2. CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS was written into the global settings
file at 05:26:11 UTC. Fourteen of fifteen live windows had started at
04:41. None of them had ever read it.
Sibling of the written-but-never-wired family (knowledge 4f13a25e) and of
scripts/wiring_gap_phase1.py, which catches a new function that no caller
calls. This catches the inverse: the function IS called, and the copy being
called is the stale one. Both are indistinguishable from working, which is
why neither is catchable by asking whether the work got done.
Adding an invariant is a data edit, not a code edit. That is deliberate --
the cost of tracking one more thing has to stay near zero or nobody will.

file_markers.name: hook-timing whose-window field
file_markers.why: Without this, every window's rows are anonymous in one shared log and no freeze census can tell two windows apart.

settings_must_be_empty.name: SessionStart stays empty (deadlock guard)
settings_must_be_empty.why: A Windows deadlock in the SessionStart path leaves the parent blocking on a hook that already exited -- the timer runs, thinking never arrives, and the stop button says 'stopping' forever because the event loop was never reached. The whole session-init chain was moved to UserPromptSubmit to escape it. One hook registered back here brings the freeze with it, and it would look like the freeze we are already hunting.

env_from_settings.name: stream idle timeout
env_from_settings.why: A window reads this once at start. Any window older than the file has never seen the value and still runs the old timeout.
